newsitem.title: CHINA: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Five Koreans on creditwatch.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Five Koreans on creditwatch.

text.p: Five Korean banks were placed on creditwatch negative on Wednesday in a further sign that Korea's banking sector's troubles are far from over.
Standard & Poor's placed five Korean banks on creditwatch negative on Wednesday.
It cited deteriorating asset quality and heightening industry risk being faced by Korean banks as defaults continue the country's highly leveraged industrial conglomerates.
S&P said it was concerned about the potential for default spillovers to other sectors of the economy, and ultimately to the banking sector.

The five banks are Hanil Bank, Korea Exchange Bank, Korea First Bank, Korea Long Term Credit Bank and Shinhan Bank, and S&P said they were among private sector creditors to the Kia group, with aggregate exposure of about 1.7 trillion won.
Korea Container Terminal Authority has issued a yen 4.3 billion samurai through Kokusai Securities. The 10-year issue carried a 2.95 percent coupon and was issued at par.
Utility blue chip Korea Electric Power Corp launched a 364-day US$500 million floating-rate note (FRN) issue.
The FRNs pay a coupon of 15 basis points over the London Interbank Offered Rate and were priced and re-offered at par. Fees are 10 basis points. SBC Warburg is lead manager.
In Hong Kong, a HK$3 billion Airport Authority (AA) three-year revolving credit launched last week is likely to be increased, bankers said.
They said the deal, which pays a margin of 30 basis points annually plus fees, would probably be increased to HK$4 billion.
The AA is a rare but popular name in the loan market -- this deal is only its second -- and its previous borrowing of HK$8.2 billion was a spectacular success early last year.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi's floating rate certificate of deposit (FRCD) issue has been upped to HK$2.5 billion.
Bankers said the deal was popular partly because the issuer planned to apply for access to a special liquidity facility, but also because of its low risk weighting.
Goldman Sachs is lead managing a 30 billion yen subordinated Eurobond for African Development Bank, which is rated Aa1/AA-minus.
The five-year bond was due to be priced later on Wednesday to yield 148 basis points over the Japanese Government bond.
